relationships.subject: VX-548
relationships.evidence_quote: a selective Nav1.8 inhibitor VX-548 (suzetrigine) has shown efficacy for treating acute pain in clinical trials

relationships.subject: VX-548
relationships.evidence_quote: Generally, repetitive firing during depolarizations was diminished but not eliminated by VX-548.

relationships.subject: Nav1.7
relationships.evidence_quote: Second, Nav1.7 current dominated during initial spikes and could also contribute to repetitive firing.

relationships.subject: Nav1.8
relationships.evidence_quote: Nav1.8 channels contribute to the later phase of the rising phase of the action potential and, because they inactivate more slowly, contribute to the shoulder of the action potential.

relationships.subject: VX-548
relationships.evidence_quote: Counterintuitively, VX-548 shortened the refractory period-likely reflecting reduced potassium channel activation by the smaller, narrower action potential-sometimes resulting in faster firing.

key_findings: 10 nM VX-548 reduced action potential peak and shoulder in human DRG neurons but barely changed threshold or upstroke, and repetitive firing persisted.
Residual firing attributed to large Nav1.8 currents (even 99% block leaves nA-level current) and Nav1.7 current, possibly explaining incomplete analgesia.
